_comment: A fallback, not a fact. Every endpoint that reports its own served window
is asked first (llama.cpp /props, Ollama /api/show, vLLM and compatible
/v1/models, Text Generation Inference /info, OpenRouter's model list); this
table answers only for the vendor APIs that publish a window but do not
serve it over an endpoint, and for an open-weight tag reached through a
proxy that says nothing. A published figure can change under a model id
without the id changing, so a wrong row is corrected either here or, per
deployment and without editing the tree, by setting
core.llm.openai.context_size to the window the server was started with.
Keys match the longest leading run of the model id, lower-cased, with any
vendor path segment in front of it and any tag after a colon removed.
Values are tokens. A model this table does not name falls back to the

max_output._comment: The maximum output each model's vendor documents, with the page it is documented on. A model is listed only when its vendor's own documentation states the figure; a model not listed that a hosted API serves takes the documented fallback. DeepSeek's Models & Pricing page writes its figure as 384K, which is 393,216 tokens.

prices._comment: What a model's tokens cost, in US dollars per million, as its vendor's own page documents them, with that page. Data for the operator's spend ceiling (core.llm.max_spend_usd_per_job), never a limit of its own: a row is read only where core.llm.model_prices names no price for the model, and a model not listed has no price. A row's own figures are its price outside every window; each window is a span of the day, UTC, on the weekdays it names, with the figures the vendor charges then, and a call is priced at the window its request was sent in. DeepSeek documents peak hours of 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, at twice the off-peak rate, and every other hour as off-peak; it does not say whether a request is timed at its start or its end. It also takes Chinese public holidays out of the peak hours, which no window here names: a call made in a peak window on such a day is priced at the peak rate, above what it cost.
